DIN computes candidate-specific interest as \(r_t(c)=\sum_{j\le t}g(e_j,e_c)e_j\), using a learned activation network; its weights need not sum to one. A reproducible normalized variant uses \(a_{jc}=\mathrm{MLP}([h_j,e_c,h_j-e_c,h_j\odot e_c])\), then \(r_t(c)=\sum_j\mathrm{softmax}_j(a_{jc}+m_{tj})h_j\). This is a design adaptation, not the original DIN formula. Set \(m_{tj}=-\infty\) for padding and \(j>t\) when predicting item \(t+1\); contextual history states must themselves be causally encoded. Return zero for empty histories. [DIN](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.06978v1), [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).

Derived computational requirements: for history length L, dimension d and N candidates, fixed-depth SASRec encodes once in O(L²d+Ld²), then scores in O(Nd). Candidate attention adds O(NLd) for dot-product attention, or O(NL(dh+h²)) for a dense activation MLP of width h. Cache history states/projections; process C candidates per chunk, normalize over history independently for each candidate, exclude seen items, and merge chunk top-k results. Attention storage becomes O(CL), although materialized interaction features can require O(CLd). Chunking preserves exhaustive ranking, up to numerical/tie handling, but reduces memory rather than total computation. Disable dropout and use fixed normalization statistics. Evaluate benchmark HR@10 on its pinned candidates; full-catalog recommendations require scoring every eligible item.

A proposed bounded extension is \(s(c)=s_0(c)+g_t e_c^T\operatorname{clipnorm}(Wr_t(c),\rho)\), with \(g_t=\epsilon\tanh(a_t)\). Initialize the gate output to zero to recover baseline scores exactly; the correction satisfies \(|s-s_0|\le\epsilon\rho\|e_c\|\). Exact preservation throughout training requires freezing the baseline and keeping the gate zero; bounded corrections alone cannot guarantee unchanged rankings or HR@10.
